items.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
[?] is the perceived benefits, usefulness and importance of something.
items.x: Value is the perceived benefits, usefulness and importance of something. Utility and warranty are qualities that contribute to value, and an outcome is a result for a stakeholder.

items.q: Nurses use a new shift-scheduling system every day, but did not define its requirements or approve its budget. Which role do the nurses perform?
items.x: A user is a person who uses services. The customer defined the requirements and owns the outcomes, and the sponsor authorized the budget.

items.q: A provider packages the same cloud product as 'Basic' for small businesses and 'Premium' for enterprises, with different features and support. What are 'Basic' and 'Premium'?
items.x: Service offerings are formal descriptions of one or more services designed for target consumer groups. One product can be the basis of several service offerings.

items.q: A provider and its customer hold quarterly reviews to discuss performance, feedback and future needs, and agree improvements. What is this an example of?
items.x: Service relationship management is the joint activity of provider and consumer to keep value co-creation going, based on agreed and available service offerings.

items.q: Which statement about outputs and outcomes is CORRECT?
o: Outputs are always more important than outcomes
A provider can deliver all agreed outputs and still fail to enable the outcomes the customer wants
Outcomes are deliverables of an activity
Outputs and outcomes mean the same thing
items.x: Outputs are deliverables of activities, and outcomes are results for stakeholders. Delivering outputs, such as reports on time, does not guarantee outcomes, such as better decisions. This is why ITIL focuses on outcomes and value.

items.q:
A company subscribes to a cloud service. Which two of the following are costs IMPOSED on the company?
1. The monthly subscription fee
2. Buying server hardware
3. Training users on the new service
4. Renting data-centre space
items.x: The subscription fee and user training are costs of consuming the service. Server hardware and data-centre rent are costs the cloud service removes from the company.

items.q:
Identify the missing word in the following sentence.
[?] is assurance that a product or service will meet agreed requirements.
items.x: Warranty is assurance that a product or service will meet agreed requirements, often expressed in terms of availability, capacity, security and continuity.

items.q: Which of the following describes the UTILITY of an HR system?
o: It is available from 07:00 to 22:00 every day
It calculates each employee's holiday entitlement automatically
It can be recovered within four hours after a disaster
items.x: Calculating holiday entitlement is functionality, so it is utility. Availability, encryption and recoverability are warranty aspects.

items.q: Users report that the email service is working but is much slower than usual. How should this be classified?
items.x: An incident is an unplanned interruption to a service or a reduction in the quality of a service. A significant slowdown is a reduction in quality, so it is an incident.

items.q: A monitoring tool records that the nightly backup completed successfully. How is this BEST described?
items.x: An event is any change of state that is significant for managing a service or CI. A successful backup is an informational event: no action is needed, but it is useful to record.

items.q: Which of the following is a CHANGE?
o: A user asks how to set up an out-of-office message
Users report that the website is down
Upgrading the database software that supports the billing service
A cause of repeated outages is identified
items.x: A change is the addition, modification or removal of anything that could have a direct or indirect effect on services. Option A is a service request, B an incident and D a problem.

items.q: Which measure BEST reflects the user experience of a service desk?
o: The number of tickets closed per agent
The number of phone lines installed
Feedback from users about how easy and satisfying it was to get help
items.x: Experience reflects how users perceive their interactions, both functionally and emotionally. Direct feedback, such as satisfaction and effort scores, captures it better than activity counts or technical metrics.

items.q: Artificial intelligence, machine learning, cloud computing and mobile solutions are examples of what within the four dimensions?
o: Technologies within the information and technology dimension
Roles within the organizations and people dimension
Contracts within the partners and suppliers dimension
Workflows within the value streams and processes dimension
items.x: The information and technology dimension covers the technologies that support products, services and their management, including AI, automation, cloud and mobile, as well as the information and knowledge needed.

items.q: A bank decides to concentrate on its core banking competencies and to obtain non-core capabilities, such as facilities management, from suppliers. Which factor influencing supplier strategy is this?
items.x: Strategic focus means some organizations prefer to concentrate on their core competency and use partners and suppliers for other needs.

items.q: A government regulation requires citizens' data to be stored within the country, which limits the cloud providers an agency can use. Which factor influencing supplier strategy is this?
items.x: External constraints such as regulation, government policy and industry codes influence which suppliers can be used and how.

items.q: Why should all four dimensions be considered in a balanced way?
o: Because each dimension is owned by a different department
Because neglecting any dimension can result in products and services that are undeliverable or do not meet expectations
Because technology is the only dimension that matters
items.x: Focusing on one dimension, typically technology, while neglecting the others, such as people, suppliers and processes, often causes products and services to fail to deliver value.

items.q: Which lifecycle activity typically creates prototypes and specifications so that ideas can be tested with users before a solution is built?
items.x: Design translates validated needs into specifications, architectures and prototypes. Prototyping with users helps make sure the product will deliver the expected utility, warranty and experience.

items.q: A team applies routine patches and adjusts capacity so that a live product stays within its agreed reliability and performance targets. Which lifecycle activity is this?
items.x: Operate keeps live products and services running to agreed performance and reliability targets through routine operational work such as monitoring, maintenance and capacity adjustments.

items.q:
Which two lifecycle activities are MOST directly involved in creating a new product version before it is moved into the live environment?
1. Build
2. Operate
3. Design
4. Support
items.x: Design defines what is to be created, and Build creates, configures and tests it. Operate and Support act on products that are already live.

items.q: Insights gathered while supporting users reveal a recurring usability issue, which is fed back into Design for the next version. What does this illustrate about the lifecycle?
o: The lifecycle is non-linear, and activities feed information back to each other
Support should not communicate with Design
Design only happens once per product
items.x: The lifecycle activities are interconnected. Learning from Support and Operate flows back into Discover and Design, which drives continual improvement of products and services.

items.q: A mobile app has all the required features, but customers find it confusing. The team prioritizes usability improvements because customers' experience matters to the value they perceive. Which guiding principle is MOST directly applied?
items.x: 'Focus on value' includes understanding customer and user experience, both its functional and emotional aspects, because experience strongly influences perceived value.

items.q: 'Apply your risk management skills' when deciding which existing practices to keep or replace is guidance for which guiding principle?
items.x: When assessing what can be reused, 'start where you are' recommends applying risk management skills and recognizing that sometimes nothing can be reused.

items.q: Which statement describes 'progress iteratively with feedback'?
o: Complete all analysis before starting any work
Organize work into smaller, manageable sections that can be executed and completed in a timely manner
Avoid changing plans once work has started
items.x: Resist the temptation to do everything at once. Even large initiatives should be carried out iteratively, with each iteration re-evaluated using feedback.

items.q: A team shows on a dashboard how much revenue is lost each day a defect remains unfixed, and the work is then prioritized quickly. Which guiding principle does this illustrate?
items.x: Insufficient visibility leads to poor decisions. Making work and its consequences visible increases urgency and gets support for action.

items.q: Integrated tools give a team end-to-end visibility of a product's performance across all the components and suppliers involved. Which guiding principle does this kind of automation especially support?
items.x: 'Automation can facilitate working holistically' is a recommendation for this principle. Integrated tooling helps teams see and manage the whole system.

items.q: A short, clear policy is adopted much more widely than the long, complicated policy it replaced. Which recommendation of 'keep it simple and practical' does this demonstrate?
o: Comprehend the whole, but do something
Easier to understand, more likely to adopt
items.x: Simple solutions are easier to understand and so more likely to be adopted, which improves outcomes.

items.q: Which is a recommendation for applying the 'optimize and automate' principle?
o: Ignore the other guiding principles while automating
Use the other guiding principles when applying this one
Optimize only after automation is complete
items.x: Applying 'optimize and automate' works best when combined with the other principles, for example focusing on value, keeping it simple and progressing iteratively.

items.q: Which of the following is a MANAGEMENT activity rather than a governance activity?
o: Setting the organization's overall risk appetite
Monitoring compliance with corporate policies at board level
Planning and running daily operations within the established policies
items.x: Governance sets direction through evaluate, direct and monitor. Management plans, builds, runs and reports on activities within that direction.

items.q: The governing body reviews regular reports on decisions made by AI tools to check that they comply with the organization's AI policy. Which governance activity is this?
items.x: Checking performance and conformance with policies is 'monitor'. AI governance applies the same evaluate, direct and monitor activities to the use of AI.

items.q: What is the purpose of the step 'What is the vision?' in the continual improvement model?
o: To make sure the improvement is aligned with the organization's vision, mission, goals and objectives
To measure the current performance of services
To celebrate the success of the improvement
items.x: The first step makes sure each improvement initiative supports the organization's direction, so that effort goes into improvements that matter.

items.q: Which statement about continual improvement registers (CIRs) is CORRECT?
o: An organization may only have one CIR
An organization can have several CIRs, for example at organization, team and practice level
A CIR records incidents and problems
Only the governing body may add ideas to a CIR
items.x: CIRs can exist at different levels. They make improvement ideas visible, and anyone can contribute ideas.

items.q: Which technique is MOST useful for the step 'Where are we now?'
o: Carrying out a baseline assessment, such as a maturity assessment or SWOT analysis
items.x: 'Where are we now?' requires an objective baseline. Maturity assessments, SWOT analysis and measurements of current performance are common techniques.

items.q: Which of the following is typically included in ITIL practice guidance?
o: Only a step-by-step procedure for each team
A list of approved software tools
Guidance for the practice across the four dimensions, with practice success factors and key metrics
The legal contract text for suppliers
items.x: ITIL practice guides describe each practice in terms of the four dimensions and include practice success factors and key metrics. They give practical guidance that organizations adapt.

items.q: What is the purpose of the service request management practice?
o: To support the agreed quality of a service by handling all pre-defined, user-initiated service requests in an effective and user-friendly manner
To minimize the negative impact of incidents
To set business-based targets for service levels
To make new features available for use
items.x: Service request management handles normal, pre-defined requests such as access, information or new equipment, ideally standardized and automated as far as possible.

items.q: How do the four dimensions relate to the ITIL value system?
o: They are one of its components
They apply only to the governance component
They should be considered for the value system as a whole and for all of its components
items.x: The four dimensions are not a component of the value system. They are perspectives that apply to the whole value system and to every product and service.

items.q: What is the overall aim of the ITIL value system?
o: To reduce the size of the IT department
To ensure that the organization continually co-creates value with all stakeholders through the use and management of products and services
To produce as many outputs as possible
To make sure all work follows a single fixed process
items.x: The value system describes how all components and activities work together to co-create value with stakeholders, flexibly and continually.

items.q: Which statement about where a value stream starts and ends is CORRECT?
o: It starts with demand or an opportunity and ends with value realized for a consumer
It starts with a project plan and ends with a project report
It starts with a supplier contract and ends with an invoice
It starts and ends inside a single team
items.x: A value stream is triggered by demand or an opportunity and ends when value is realized by the consumer. Along the way it often crosses teams, practices and organizations.

items.q: What does value stream MANAGEMENT add to value stream mapping?
o: It replaces the need to understand the current state
It focuses only on reducing headcount
Continual measurement and improvement of the flow of value over time, not just a one-off map
It is only used for software development
items.x: Mapping gives a picture at a point in time. Value stream management keeps measuring flow, for example lead time and flow efficiency, and improves it continually.

items.q: In the ITIL AI Capability Model, which capability is MOST concerned with making information and AI outputs clear and understandable, for example by summarizing or explaining them?
items.x: Clarification makes information and AI reasoning understandable to people, for example by summarizing a long incident history or explaining a recommendation. Transparency supports trust and governance.

items.q: Which statement BEST describes COBIT?
o: A project management method for small projects
A framework for the governance and management of enterprise information and technology
items.x: COBIT, from ISACA, focuses on governance and management of enterprise I&T. It complements ITIL, which gives more detailed guidance on managing products and services.
